c.tagline: Seat of Dutch government, grand palaces, and a North Sea beach.

taxi.fareNote: Metered; official taxis carry a blue licence plate. Booking apps are common.

emergency.note: 112 is the single EU emergency number for police, ambulance and fire in the Netherlands.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets around Hollands Spoor station and on packed Scheveningen beach in summer.

hood_desc: The historic core around the Binnenhof parliament, the Mauritshuis, the Passage arcade and Noordeinde Palace; walkable and packed with the city's must-see sights.
The Hague's lively seaside resort with a long sandy beach, a Victorian pier, the Kurhaus and a boulevard of restaurants and bars; the go-to spot for sun, surf and going out by the water.
An elegant early-20th-century residential quarter of stately townhouses halfway between the centre and the beach, near the Gemeentemuseum; calm and genteel.
A trendy, compact neighbourhood of independent cafes, brunch spots, boutiques and a Saturday organic market; popular with young professionals and creatives.
A leafy, distinguished district of embassies and villas near the Peace Palace and Panorama Mesdag; quiet, upmarket and green.

water.note: Dutch tap water is excellent and safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Trams and RandstadRail run roughly 6am-midnight; night buses cover the city and the beach into the small hours on Friday and Saturday nights.
transit.pay: Tap a contactless debit/credit card or phone on trams, RandstadRail and buses via OVpay, or use a rechargeable OV-chipkaart. Fares are distance-based, roughly €1-4 (~US$1-4.30) for a typical city trip. RandstadRail lines link the centre with Scheveningen beach and on to Rotterdam.

air: Amsterdam Schiphol (AMS) — ~30 min by direct train

tip.r: ~5–10% for good service; rounding up is common

food.name: Hollandse Nieuwe Haring
food.desc: Raw, lightly cured North Sea herring with chopped onion and pickles, taken by the tail or in a soft white bun. Peak season starts in June.

places.name: Simonis aan de Haven
places.note: Long-established Scheveningen fish house right by the boats; the classic Hague herring stop.

places.name: Haringkraam op het Plein
places.note: City-centre herring cart among the terraces, handy between the Binnenhof and Mauritshuis.

places.name: Haagse Markt
places.note: Huge open-air market with several fish stalls selling herring at local prices.

food.name: Kibbeling and Lekkerbek
food.desc: Battered chunks of cod deep-fried and served with garlic or remoulade sauce; lekkerbek is the same fish left whole in one crisp fillet.

places.name: Simonis aan de Haven
places.note: Fries fish all day beside the harbour; large portions and reliably fresh cod.

places.name: Scheveningen Boulevard Fish Stalls
places.note: Row of visstandjes along the promenade for kibbeling with a sea view.

places.name: Haagse Markt
places.note: Market fish fryers do cheap kibbeling cones, busiest on market mornings.

food.name: Indonesian Rijsttafel
food.desc: The Hague is the home of Dutch-Indonesian cooking - a rijsttafel spreads a dozen or more small dishes, from rendang to sambal goreng, around a bowl of rice.

places.name: Garoeda
places.note: One of the oldest Indonesian restaurants in the Netherlands, serving rijsttafel since the 1940s.

places.name: Warung Mini
places.note: Well-loved neighbourhood warung for hearty Javanese-Surinamese plates at fair prices.

places.name: Tokos on the Javastraat and Frederik Hendriklaan
places.note: Indonesian tokos selling ready-made rendang, satay and sambals to take away.

food.name: Poffertjes
food.desc: Tiny yeasted buckwheat pancakes cooked in a dimpled iron pan, served hot under a slab of butter and a snowfall of icing sugar.

places.name: Poffertjeskraam, Grote Markt
places.note: Market-square pancake stall; the traditional place to eat poffertjes in town.

places.name: Scheveningen Boulevard Stalls
places.note: Seafront pancake kiosks turning out poffertjes and stroopwafels all season.

places.name: Haagse Markt
places.note: Sweet stalls make poffertjes and fresh stroopwafels alongside the food aisles.

food.name: Bitterballen
food.desc: Crumbed, deep-fried balls of rich beef ragout with sharp mustard - the Dutch bar snack, ordered with a beer in any brown cafe.

places.name: Cafe de Oude Mol
places.note: Tiny, atmospheric brown cafe in the old centre; classic bitterballen-and-beer spot.

places.name: De Zwarte Ruiter
places.note: Landmark grand cafe on the square with a big terrace and a full bar-snack menu.

places.name: Cafe de Paas
places.note: Renowned Hague beer cafe with a long Dutch beer list to go with the snacks.

food.name: Erwtensoep (Snert)
food.desc: Split pea soup thick enough to stand a spoon in, with smoked sausage and pork, served with rye bread and bacon in winter.

places.name: Cafe de Paas
places.note: Traditional Dutch cafe cooking; snert in the cold months with local beer.

places.name: Cafe de Oude Mol
places.note: Old-school brown cafe menu where winter soups are done properly.

places.name: Haagse Markt
places.note: Market food stalls sell hot snert by the cup on winter market days.

food.name: Jenever
food.desc: Dutch juniper spirit, drunk cold and neat from a tulip glass, often as a kopstootje chaser alongside a beer.

places.name: Van Kleef Distillery
places.note: Historic Hague distillery and tasting room dating to 1842, with dozens of jenevers and liqueurs.

places.name: Cafe de Paas
places.note: Beer cafe that also keeps a proper jenever selection for the kopstootje.

places.name: Cafe de Oude Mol
places.note: Brown cafe where a jenever with a beer is the standard order.

food.name: Hague Craft Beer
food.desc: The city has its own brewing scene, led by Kompaan in the Binckhorst, plus a deep bench of Dutch and Belgian taps in the old beer cafes.

places.name: Kompaan Beer Bar
places.note: Taproom of The Hague's best-known brewery, with food trucks and a big terrace.

places.name: Cafe de Paas
places.note: Long-standing specialist beer cafe with a canal-side terrace.

places.name: De Zwarte Ruiter
places.note: Central grand cafe on the busiest square for an easy pint.

landmarks: Binnenhof and Ridderzaal
The Gothic heart of Dutch democracy for eight centuries, this turreted parliamentary complex around the Hall of Knights rises photogenically beside the Hofvijver pond.
Mauritshuis
An intimate 17th-century palace-museum whose golden-age treasures include Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring and Rembrandt's Anatomy Lesson of Dr Tulp.
Peace Palace (Vredespaleis)
Seat of the International Court of Justice, this neo-Renaissance palace of 1913 symbolises world peace with its soaring clock tower and gift-filled interiors.
Scheveningen Beach and Pier
The Netherlands' most famous seaside resort pairs a broad sandy beach with a landmark pier featuring a Ferris wheel, bungee tower and buzzing boulevard.
Panorama Mesdag
Step inside Europe's largest surviving circular painting, a dizzying 120-metre canvas from 1881 that immerses viewers in the dunes of old Scheveningen.
Madurodam
The entire Netherlands shrunk to 1:25 scale, this beloved miniature park recreates canals, windmills and Schiphol Airport in charming, interactive detail.
Escher in Het Paleis
A former royal winter palace on Lange Voorhout devoted to M.C. Escher's mind-bending prints, complete with impossible staircases and playful optical-illusion rooms.
Kunstmuseum Den Haag
Berlage's art-deco masterpiece houses the world's largest Mondrian collection, culminating in the unfinished Victory Boogie Woogie, plus superb fashion and Delftware galleries.
Noordeinde Palace
King Willem-Alexander's working palace presides over an elegant shopping street; admire its classical facade, equestrian statue and the palace gardens hidden behind.
Louwman Museum
One of the world's finest private car collections displays over 250 automobiles, from 1880s pioneers to James Bond's Aston Martin, in a striking purpose-built museum.

train.note: Direct international trains from The Hague are limited - most journeys mean a 25-minute hop to Rotterdam Centraal and a change onto Eurostar for Brussels, Paris or London. Den Haag Centraal and Den Haag HS both take intercity services; Amsterdam is under an hour and Schiphol airport 30 minutes. NS domestic fares are fixed-price, but international tickets are cheaper booked early.

bus.note: Coaches stop at Den Haag Centraal and at the Hollands Spoor station. FlixBus and BlaBlaCar Bus cover the European network; Brussels takes about 3 hours. Carry your passport for UK-bound services, which include a full immigration check at the Channel.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry from The Hague - Scheveningen harbour is a fishing and marina port. The North Sea crossings leave from Hook of Holland, about 30 minutes away by the RandstadRail metro, where Stena Line sails to Harwich, and from IJmuiden and Rotterdam Europoort.
